chapter: Bostic, Washington clubs and arriving in New York
title: Little Harlem drummers Streamline and Al Dunn
summary: Brower asks about Washington drummers; Cobb describes Streamline and Al "Gotta Be" Dunn.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Do you remember a drummer named Streamline?

Streamline, yeah. Streamline was a guy that stammered. He couldn’t get one word out for maybe five minutes, but he could sing “The green grass grows all around, the green grass grows all around” and not miss a beat. I never could understand that. He used to have to sit up there and sing. When he’d come down and try to talk to you, he’d be trying to get a word out. Good guy though. I loved him.
Yeah, Streamline. Good drummer and singer – entertainer. That’s what Streamline was.
Al “Gotta Be” Dunn was a good one too. He was like a – Al Dunn at that time, he was like a pimp playing the drums. He looked like a – he dressed like that, and he played with his hand over like that.

No, just like this. Not matched hands, but with his hand turned over like that. He’d make rim shots like that. Like, what do you play? He’d play like that. I just looked at it. It looked funny to me, but it was perfect for him. He was one of the guys. He was a hard hustler. He would go around and hustle up gigs for his band. I used to admire him, because he was a great hustling guy. He can play good.
